text: . In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by 50 paise to close at 95 rupees and 28 paise against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 102.27 in intra-day trade.

. Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia have been advised to remain calm, vigilant and stay indoors in case of an aerial attack, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said today as it opened a 24×7 control room to assist the community. The embassy also strongly advised Indian nationals to refrain from circulating or reposting any videos or news related to the ongoing events.Indian nationals were advised to remain in regular contact with their airlines and verify the latest status of their flights. Those in an emergency who wish to leave Saudi Arabia may avail flights from airports in neighbouring Gulf countries, particularly Qatar and Bahrain, subject to obtaining visas as per their rules, the Embassy said.Giving an update on the Indian nationals injured in the October 10 attack on Riyadh airport, the Embassy stated that four people remain in the ICU, four are receiving medical care in the normal ward, and three have been discharged.Consulate General of India in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia has also issued an advisory in view of the ongoing flight disruptions, urging Indian nationals, particularly Umrah pilgrims travelling through Jeddah and Madinah, to regularly check their flight status with their respective airlines. They have been asked to stay in contact with their travel agents and Umrah service providers. The Consulate General has established a 24×7 Control Room to assist affected Indian nationals. The contact details are +966 12 2614093 and +966 556122301. The Whatsapp number is +966 536209704 and the email is pbskcgi@gmail.com.On October 10, Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said that the attack targeting King Khalid International Airport on Saturday afternoon killed 12 people and injured 309 others.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised India’s GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent for 2026-27, up from 6.4 per cent in July.  In its flagship World Economic Outlook report, the IMF said the revision in the estimate comes on the back of stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity.  It said India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favourable demographic dynamics, an expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms. The revision came after the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) latest monetary policy meeting, which raised its GDP growth estimate for the current financial year to 7.1 per cent. The IMF has also lifted its FY28 growth projection for India by 0.3 percentage points to 7%, pointing to the durability of the country’s expansion.

. Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh today visited the Oil Refinery Construction site at Altanshiree Soum in Mongolia’s Dornogobi Province and thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for India’s unwavering support for the strategically important project.According to the India Embassy in Ulaanbaatar, Khurelsukh expressed satisfaction with the progress of the strategically important project, which is expected to enable Mongolia to produce its own refined fuel.During the visit, he also interacted with the engineers and workers involved in the construction and appreciated Indian Ambassador to Mongolia Atul Malhari Gotsurve’s role in advancing the project.During Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Mongolia in 2015, a Line of Credit (LOC) of one billion US dollar was approved for development of infrastructure, which the Government of Mongolia decided to utilise for construction of its first-ever oil refinery in Dornogobi Province with a capacity of 1.5 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA).

. India’s Udhayveer Sidhu clinched the gold medal in the men’s 10-metre air pistol event at the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF), World Cup Rifle and Pistol in Cairo, Egypt, today. The 24-year-old shooter delivered an impressive performance in the medal match, scoring 240.6 points to defeat Germany’s multi-Olympic medallist Christian Reitz by a narrow margin of 0.5 points.Olympic bronze medallists Swapnil Suresh Kusale and Sarabjot Singh are among the leading members of the 24-strong Indian contingent at the tournament, which continues until the 16th of this month. India is competing in eight individual Olympic disciplines and two mixed-team events, with a contingent comprising experienced Olympians and promising young shooters.

. The Government has the draft National Steel Policy-Vision 2047, which provides a long-term policy framework to build a globally competitive, technologically advanced, environmentally sustainable and resource-efficient steel sector. The Policy aims to meet the country’s growing steel requirements while strengthening India’s position in the global steel industry. The policy projects the country’s per capita steel consumption rising to 302 kilograms from the current 116 kilograms, while India’s crude steel production has already increased from 89 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 170 million tonnes in 2025-26. The Policy also projects an increase in the country’s steel exports to 45 MT by 2047. Further, it says that India aims for a near threefold expansion in crude steel-making capacity to 604 million tonnes by 2047 and to raise finished steel demand to 505 million tonnes.The draft Policy focuses on promoting greater use of steel in infrastructure, housing, transportation, renewable energy, and emerging manufacturing sectors. It also places emphasis on cleaner steel production, seeking to lower average emissions intensity from 2.54 tonnes of carbon dioxide per tonne of crude steel to 1.54 tonnes by 2047 through measures including greater energy efficiency, renewable electricity, increased scrap use and hydrogen-based steel-making.

. In Badminton, India’s Anmol Kharb has won the Women’s Singles title at the Türkiye International Challenge. She defeated her compatriot Aakarshi Kashyap in straight games, 21-11, 21-14 in the final. This marks Anmol’s third international senior title. Meanwhile, India’s Suraj Goala and Nicholas Raj finished runners-up at the Men’s Doubles event. The Indian pair lost to Denmark’s William Kryger Boe and Rasmus Espersen in the final, 14-21, 19-21.

. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India next week to strengthen energy cooperation and strategic partnership between the two countries. US State Department said, Mr Rubio will travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar during his tour. State Department said, he will meet with senior government officials to strengthen India-US strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. Mr Rubio will also meet business leaders to promote investment and economic cooperation. This will be Mr Rubio’s second visit to India since May, when he attended the Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting hosted by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi.Before arriving in India, Mr Rubio will participate in the C5+1 Ministerial meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The meeting will focus on how strategic cooperation through the diplomatic platform can promote a more peaceful and prosperous future for the US and Central Asian countries. Mr Rubio will also hold bilateral meetings with senior officials from the five Central Asian countries – Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. A US commercial delegation comprising more than 200 business leaders will accompany Mr Rubio to promote stronger commercial cooperation between the US and Central Asia.

. The AYUSH Ministry has issued standard treatment guidelines on Management of Dermatological Disorders for Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy, with the inclusion of Yoga. The document has been prepared by the Ayush Vertical of the Directorate General of Health Services and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Ministry said that the document is intended to bring more uniformity, quality assurance and evidence-informed practice to clinical care across the Ayush systems. Ayush Minister Prataprao Jadhav underlined that these guidelines will deepen the integration of Ayush systems with the national healthcare framework. He said that by promoting standardised and evidence-informed clinical practice, the guiidelines will contribute to improving patient care and strengthening the role of Ayush systems in public health.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has said two Bangladeshis have been killed and more than 24 are receiving treatment in hospitals in Riyadh amid the ongoing conflict in Saudi Arabia. Several injured Bangladeshis are in intensive care. Speaking to journalists in Dhaka, she called for an immediate end to the conflict, expressing concern over civilian casualties and the humanitarian situation. According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh, ten flights have been affected, disrupting the travel plans of thousands of passengers.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said the Government is open to hearing suggestions on the removal of long-term capital gains tax during consultations for the upcoming Union Budget. Ms Sithraman said this while speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today. The Finance Minister noted that investors, both in India and overseas, had been discussing the taxation of capital gains and different asset classes, including the securities transaction tax. She added that the government will continue to follow a disciplined fiscal approach while protecting spending on key areas such as welfare, education and healthcare.On India’s semiconductor strategy, Ms Sitharaman said the country is pursuing opportunities in both advanced chips and semiconductors used in everyday products. She underlined that the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and data centres will increase the need for electricity generation and reliable power infrastructure. Further, the Minister stressed the importance of developing sustainable green energy sources to meet the growing power requirements of data centres, semiconductor manufacturing and other AI-related infrastructure.

. India have set a target of 224 runs for the West Indies in the third T20 International at Holkar Stadium in Indore. Put into bat, India were all out for 223 runs in the allotted 20 overs. Abhishek Sharma played a superb 69 runs off 30 balls.In reply, West Indies were 16 for 1 in 3 overs, when reports last came in.The five-match series is currently level at one match apiece, after West Indies defeated India by six wickets in the second T20 International in Ranchi on Friday evening. India had defeated West Indies by eight wickets in the opening T20 in Lucknow.

. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that India-US trade talks are heading in the right direction and a deal is being ironed out currently. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Dr Jaishankar informed that trade ministers of the two countries are working on it and both nations are pretty far advanced in the process of negotiations for the trade deal.Replying to a query, Dr Jaishankar emphasised that the US has repositioned itself and every country has to recalibrate and reset its relationship with the US. He highlighted that India has a strong Strategic Partnership with the US.In China, the External Affairs Minister maintained that the bilateral relationship will have consequences if peace and tranquillity in border areas are disturbed. He stated that the relationship is moving towards normalcy as the border areas are settling down. He noted that India and China have been able to restore peace and tranquillity in border areas.Dr Jaishankar remarked that the trade balance between India and China is completely tilted and is extremely one-sided. He said India is not getting a level playing field in China.Replying to another query on Russia, Dr Jaishankar clearly pointed out that India has never encountered a whiff of a suggestion that anything India is procuring from Russia comes with Chinese tech. He opined that because of the Ukraine war, Russia has turned much more to Asia. He said that it is in India’s interest, and the world’s interest, that Russia has multiple choices. He said India is a natural option in that regard.

Facing criticism over the diesel deal with Russia, US President Donald Trump defended a deal to release Russian diesel into global markets, saying it is intended to ease high fuel prices and is not meant for the United States. Trump said last Friday that Russia will supply more than 3 lakh tons of diesel, followed by 5 lakh tons in November and 1 million tons thereafter. The US Treasury Department issued a temporary license easing sanctions on Russian diesel shipments until April 7, 2027.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over  Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Punjab, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for tomorrow. Similar weather conditions are expected over Andhra Pradesh and West Rajasthan.  IMD said that conditions are likely to become favourable for further withdrawal of southwest monsoon from some more parts of eastern India and many parts of northeast India during the next two days. Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Kerala can also experience thunderstorms accompanied with Lightning.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address ‘Brihattar Bharat: International Conference on ‘Bharat’s Cultural Connections across the Globe’ in New Delhi today through a video message.The three-day conference will bring together delegates, ambassadors and scholars from 50 nations to deliberate on India’s historical and contemporary cultural connections with the wider world. Participants from countries including China, Japan, Mongolia, Nepal and Iran, among others, will contribute to discussions on shared cultural heritage and civilizational exchanges. The conference marks the centenary of the Greater India Society, also known as Brihattar Bharat Parishad, established in Kolkata on 14 October 1926 by a generation of Indian scholars, with Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore as its spiritual guide. An exhibition titled ‘Common Cultural Heritage of Asia’ will be organised during the conference.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.

. India’s Anandkumar Velkumar has won bronze in the 500-metre sprint at the World Skate Games 2026 in  Asunción, Paraguay, adding another medal to his expanding collection on the international speed skating stage. The 23-year-old speed skater from Tamil Nadu finished on the podium in 40.856 seconds, continuing his incredible run following his unprecedented accomplishments at the 2025 World Speed Skating Championships. Velkumar had earned bronze in the 500m and gold in the 1000m and marathon in the 2025 championships as well, making him a two-time world champion.His most recent podium result enhances India’s standing in elite speed skating and highlights his consistency over long distances. Velkumar has become one of the nation’s most well-known figures in the sport thanks to his performances.Earlier, Kerala’s Anirudhan Vinod won silver in the junior men’s 200m Dual Time Trial at the Games.Vinod clocked 17.658 seconds, finishing just 0.043 seconds behind Colombia’s Emanuel Ramos Mosquera, who won gold in 17.615 seconds. Chinese Taipei’s Wei-Ning Chuang secured bronze in 17.718 seconds.

. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand arrived in New Delhi on a two day visit to India this evening. During her visit, she will meet External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Minister Jayant Chaudhary tomorrow. The External Affairs Ministry informed that this is Minister Anand’s third visit to India since June 2025, reflecting the sustained high-level engagement and positive momentum in India-Canada relations. The Ministry added that the visit will provide an opportunity for both sides to build on the recent progress and further advance India-Canada bilateral partnership.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended over one and a half per cent higher today. The Sensex surged 1,109 points to close at 73,034. The Nifty soared 359 points to settle at 22,722.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index climbed over one per cent while the Smallcap 100 index eked out a marginal gain of 0.1 per cent.

. Indian opener Shafali Verma was named the ‘ICC Women’s Player of the Month’ winner for September 2026, following incredible title-winning outings in the Women’s Asia Cup and the Asian Games with the bat and clutch contributions in high-stakes matches. On the other hand, Indian captain Shubman Gill was named ICC men’s Player of the Month for a record fifth time following his outstanding performance in the One Day International series against the West Indies.It is the second time Shafali has won the monthly award, with the 22-year-old first tasting success in November last year when she helped India claim the ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup on home soil, as per the ICC. Shafali Verma, was the highest run-scorer for her team as India won the Women’s Asia Cup.Shubman Gill, as per the ICC, won the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma of India and Zimbabwe’s Sikandar Raza. Gill scored 333 runs in India’s first two One Day Internationals against West Indies, with a century in the opener and an unbeaten double century in the second. India won both matches by eight wickets. This is Gill’s fifth ICC Men’s Player of the Month award, after wins in January 2023, September 2023, February 2025 and July 2025, extending his record as the men’s player with the most wins.

. President Droupadi Murmu will arrive in Vijayawada today on a two-day visit to Andhra Pradesh. She will inaugurate the National Saras Mela 2026 tomorrow.“The President will offer prayers at Sri Kanaka Durga Temple in Vijayawada this evening. Tomorrow, she will inaugurate the National Saras Mela 2026 in Vijayawada. The mela is being organised by the Union Ministry of Rural Development in association with the Government of Andhra Pradesh. More than one thousand five hundred women members of Self-Help Groups from over thirty States and Union Territories are participating in the mela. The SARAS Mela 2026 helps women entrepreneurs showcase their traditional crafts, reach wider markets and sell their products to customers across the country.

. The Saudi-led Coalition has urged civilians to evacuate the Yemeni Oil Company’s Al-Sabah Central Station in Sana’a ahead of what it described as a planned “qualitative operation”. The Coalition’s Joint Forces Command issued the warning, asking civilians to leave the designated site in accordance with an illustrative map they shared.Shortly after this statement, the Houthis reportedly warned Saudi Arabia of a tough response if they hit Sana’a. The Houthi military warned employees and citizens located near any Aramco oil facility to evacuate and stay away from them. They said these facilities are legitimate targets, as reported by Houthi-affiliated Saba News Agency (Sana’a branch).Saudi Arabia intercepted and destroyed three unmanned aerial vehicles north of Riyadh, while two ballistic missiles launched towards Khamis Mushait were also intercepted, informed Coalition spokesman Major General Turki Al-Malki.Air India, Air India Express, Akasa Air and IndiGo have extended flight cancellations to and from several Saudi cities including Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah, until October 17, citing the prevailing situation.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh has advised Indian nationals to remain calm and vigilant, follow instructions from local authorities, stay indoors during aerial attacks and refrain from circulating videos or unverified news about the ongoing events. The Embassy, the Indian Consulate in Jeddah and their VFS passport and attestation services continue to operate normally. While operations at Riyadh airport remain suspended, flights at Dammam, Jeddah and Madinah airports are continuing but passengers may face disruptions at these airports.

. Denmark Open Badminton tournament kicks off in Odense today. Two-time Olympic medalist P V Sindhu will take on Yvonne Li of Germany in the Women’s Singles round of 32 match while Tanvi Sharma will be up against Natsuki Nidaira of Japan today. Sindhu will be joined in the women’s singles draw by compatriots Ashmita Chaliha, Devika Sihag and Unnati Hooda.In Men’s Singles, Lakshya Sen and former world number one Kidambi Srikanth will be in action today in the round of 32 matches. India’s Ayush Shetty will also be in action. In Men’s Doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will be in action. World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will lead India’s challenge in women’s doubles alongside Rutaparna Panda and Swetaparna Panda.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through projects such as the Dholera Special Investment Region.Most industrial towns grow first and get wired later. Dholera is Prime Minister Modi’s bold new vision: a brand-new smart city on the Gulf of Khambhat where roads, water, power, and internet are built before a single plot is sold. India’s first semiconductor fabrication factory is coming up right here in this space.Sharing his pride in Dholera’s rapid growth as a modern manufacturing hub, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said:Elaborating on the scale of the smart city and its rapidly advancing infrastructure, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel said:Rising from historic maritime roots to pioneer India’s high-tech manufacturing future, Dholera stands as a shining testament to visionary planning and a Viksit Bharat.

. In cricket, India defeated the West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20 International at the Holkar Stadium in Indore last night.Chasing a target of 224 runs, the West Indies managed to score 209 for seven in their stipulated 20 overs. Shimron Hetmyer was the top scorer with 43 runs, while Kamil Pooran scored 42. For India, Arshdeep Singh took three wickets.Earlier, the West Indies won the toss and opted to bowl. Batting first, India were bowled out for 223 in 20 overs. Abhishek Sharma played a superb knock of 69 runs off 30 balls. For the West Indies, Roston Chase, Shamar Joseph and Shamar Springer took two wickets each. Arshdeep Singh was adjudged Player of the Match.India had defeated the West Indies by eight wickets in the opening T20 International in Lucknow. In the second match on Friday, the West Indies beat India by six wickets in Ranchi to level the series. With last night’s victory, India now lead the five-match series 2-1.The fourth match of the series will be played the day after tomorrow at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi index plunged 5.5 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.9 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 1.8 per cent. On the other hand, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng and Singapore’s Strait Times rose 0.3 per cent each and China’s Shanghai Composite added 0.1 per cent.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 added nearly 0.6 per cent while, Germany’s DAX gained 0.3 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 1.8 per cent lower at 104 US dollars and 72 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading two per cent lower at 91 US dollars and 84 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. The Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Northern Emirates have cautioned Indian nationals against fraudulent visa and migration processing agencies operating outside India, including in the UAE.In a joint-advisory, the mission and the post said they had received complaints against agencies promoting third-country employment and residency visa services through social media advertisements, collecting fees from applicants and subsequently failing to deliver the promised services or provide refunds.Indian nationals have been advised to exercise utmost caution and not rely solely on social media advertisements or blindly trust private visa processing agencies, especially those operating from outside India.The advisory also urged people to verify visa requirements, application procedures and authorised channels for obtaining employment or residency visas directly with the embassy or consulate of the country of intended visit.The advisory further cautioned applicants against making payments based on promises of visa approval, stressing that no agency can guarantee a visa, as the decision rests solely with the issuing government.For accurate and updated visa information, applicants are advised to consult the official government or embassy websites of the country concerned rather than relying on third-party sources.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today felicitated sportspersons from the three Services for winning 27 medals at the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan. The athletes won six gold, eleven silver and ten bronze medals, contributing significantly to India’s overall tally of 85 medals andfourth-place finish. Addressing the athletes, Mr Singh praised their discipline, hard work and team spirit. He lauded the Mission Olympic Wing, coaches and support staff for their role in identifying and nurturing sporting talent.Defence Minister reiterated the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led Government’s commitment to strengthening India’s sporting ecosystem, with sustained focus on infrastructure, modern training facilities and better opportunities for athletes.The Defence Minister also urged the athletes and trainers to adopt a focused approach towards the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, expressing confidence that the Services would deliver an even stronger performance.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has emphasized that India and ASEAN share a clear interest in a peaceful, stable, and open Indo-Pacific region. Addressing the ASEAN-India Defence Think Tank Forum in New Delhi this morning, Mr Singh said that ASEAN is central to India’s Indo-Pacific vision and that India’s Act East Policy is a long-term commitment to working with Southeast Asia as an equal partner.Mr. Singh highlighted that the Indian Ocean and the waters of Southeast Asia constitute a single connected maritime space, making its safety a shared responsibility. Pointing to the designation of 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, he called for strengthening maritime domain awareness, improving information sharing, and building collective capabilities to respond to emergencies, piracy, and illegal fishing.Outlining practical steps for the forum, Mr Singh proposed developing a joint India-ASEAN research agenda focused on maritime security, disaster response, cyber threats, and emerging technologies. He also suggested initiating pilot projects, such as tabletop exercises on maritime disaster response and joint studies on counter-drone solutions, alongside promoting Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues to sustain discussions.On the front of defence cooperation, Mr. Singh invited ASEAN nations to collaborate on technologies like artificial intelligence, drones, and space-based systems. He noted that India’s ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ initiative presents opportunities for trusted partners in the co-development, co-production, and maintenance of defence equipment, including patrol vessels, radars, and air defence systems.Highlighting the historical context, the Minister noted that ancient Indian kingdoms, including the Cholas and Pallavas, maintained trade and maritime links with Southeast Asia, providing a strong foundation for today’s modern partnership. He observed that think tanks play a vital role in this process by helping governments understand mutual concerns and offering actionable options before challenges escalate into crises.

. The First BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting concluded in New Delhi with the adoption of the Delhi Declaration. In the declaration, the BIMSTEC Nations have strongly condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism. In the declaration, the BIMSTEC nations reiterated their determination to prevent, combat and eliminate terrorism and violent extremism conducive to terrorism in a comprehensive and sustained manner, in accordance with the UN Charter and international law. They also reaffirmed commitment to strengthening regional cooperation under BIMSTEC for realizing a connected, secure, resilient, developed and prosperous BIMSTEC region. They also expressed deepest condolences and solidarity with the victims of terrorist attacks in Member States and their families and with the Governments of the affected States. The nations called for those responsible to be brought to justice in accordance with applicable domestic and international law. The Delhi Declaration also called for effective implementation of the finalized Plans of Action in areas of Human Trafficking, Narcotic Drugs and Precursor Chemicals and Anti-Money Laundering, as well as finalisation of the Plan of Action by the Sub-Group on Cooperation in Countering Radicalization and Terrorism. It also called for effective implementation of the BIMSTEC Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters, which was signed in March 2022 at the 5th BIMSTEC Summit in Colombo. The BIMSTEC nations also reaffirmed the principle that cooperation within BIMSTEC in the security sector is based on respect for the principle of sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, non-aggression, peaceful co-existence and mutual respect.

. India’s internet subscriber base has risen to over 111 crore 41 lakh at the end of June this year, from around 109 crore 28 lakh at the end of March 2026, registering a quarterly growth rate of 96%. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), in its Indian Telecom Services Performance Indicator Report noted that of the total internet subscribers, more than four crore seventy-seven lakh were wired internet subscribers and around one hundred six crore sixty-four lakh were wireless internet subscribers. The Internet subscriber base is comprised of Broadband Internet subscriber base and Narrowband Internet subscriber base. According to the report, the broadband Internet subscriber base increased by 2.03% and the narrowband Internet subscriber base decreased by 0.89% at the end of June 2026. The report also highlighted the growth in India’s telephone subscribers, which increased from around 133 crore at the end of March 2026 to 134 crore at the end of June 2026, registering quarterly growth of 1.31%. India’s overall tele-density also rose from 93.26% at the end of March 2026 to 94.31% at the end of June 2026.

. The Sports Ministry has removed para-shooting coach Jai Prakash Nautiyal from India’s contingent for the Para Asian Games amid allegations of selection irregularities and demands for an investigation. Long-serving national coach Jeevan L. Rai will replace him. The ministry has also approved 166 athletes for the Para Asian Games, which will begin on October 18 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. India won a record 108 medals, including 27 gold, at the previous edition of the Para Asian Games, crossing the 100-medal mark for the first time.

. The Prime Ministers Museum and Library (PMML) will open a new visitor kiosk today at Block-I of Teen Murti Bhawan in New Delhi. The chairman of the Executive Committee, Nripendra Misra, will formally inaugurate the kiosk. The visitor-friendly initiative provides dedicated facilities to cater to the large and growing number of visitors to the Sangrahalaya.Designed with convenience and accessibility in mind, the kiosk will offer a range of refreshments and quick bites to enhance the visitor experience, particularly for families and young people. It will stock over 400 Amul products, including popular dairy items and snacks, to cater to diverse tastes. The partnership with Amul aims to provide visitors with high-quality, familiar options while ensuring a comfortable and welcoming environment within the museum complex.

. Saudi Arabia has extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh as authorities continue safety inspections following deadly attacks over the weekend. Saudi Arabia also reported a fresh threat involving drones and cruise missiles on Monday.The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said the suspension would remain in place while procedures to verify the safety and operational readiness of airport facilities were completed in coordination with the relevant authorities. The extension follows attacks on the airport on October 10 and 11 that killed 14 people and injured hundreds, disrupting air travel and prompting airlines to cancel or suspend services to Saudi Arabia. Several international carriers announced further flight suspensions on Monday, adding to travel disruption across the region.Major General Turki Al-Malki, official spokesman for the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen, said a threat involving drones and cruise missiles against Saudi Arabia had been detected and tracked and was being dealt with. Earlier in the day, the Coalition had posted that a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait had been intercepted and destroyed.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said the family of Mohammed Yousuf Ali, an Indian national who died in the October 10 attack, had decided to hold his funeral in Riyadh. The mission said it was assisting the family with the required formalities. In an update posted on social media, the embassy said three injured Indian nationals remained in intensive care and two more had been admitted to the ICU. Two others were in regular hospital wards, while the remaining injured nationals had been discharged. Embassy officials had visited hospitals treating injured nationals, and the mission said it remained in contact with their families and was providing assistance.The security situation has added urgency to discussions on protecting energy infrastructure and maintaining reliable supplies across the Gulf. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said on Monday that energy security could not be taken for granted, warning that the current circumstances had tested Saudi Arabia’s infrastructure, institutions and resilience. He made the remarks at the 25th WPC Energy Congress, an international gathering of energy policymakers and industry representatives taking place in Riyadh. The conference has continued despite the airport attacks. The minister also reportedly outlined plans to increase Saudi Arabia’s capacity to export crude oil through pipelines to as much as 10 million barrels per day over the next two to three years.The attacks on the civilian infrastructure have also prompted widespread condemnation and calls for a coordinated regional response. Dr. Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said the security of Gulf countries was indivisible and described collective security as a shared responsibility.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

These areas include trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties. Both leaders had a warm and productive conversation today. . The UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant transactions will be implemented after Diwali. In a social media post, National Payments Corporation of India said that UPI and Services Steering Committee today decided that, keeping in mind the festive season, MDR on select Person-to-Merchant UPI transactions will be implemented immediately post Diwali.

. In Nepal, more than 100 foreign trekkers are stranded at various locations after flooding over the weekend swept away hiking trails and bridges in the country’s central region. Authorities rescued 321 people, including 12 foreigners, today after a pre-dawn landslide in Gorkha district, about 100 kilometres west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering downstream flooding. The army said rescue operations would continue tomorrow, even as the river’s water level receded. The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, which was affected by a catastrophic flood in August following a glacier collapse in another tributary. The disaster killed 1,457 people, while thousands remain missing. No fatalities were reported in the latest flooding.

India has called for greater access to finance, technology transfer and capacity-building to accelerate the implementation of Sustainable Development Goals, with poverty eradication remaining a key priority.Delivering India’s statement at the UN General Assembly’s Second Committee discussion on Sustainable Development, Counsellor Soumya Nair highlighted the country’s progress in clean energy, noting that non-fossil fuel sources now account for 55 per cent of India’s installed electricity generation capacity. She also highlighted India’s early warning capabilities and its offer to host the Fourth UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction in 2030.Ms Nair underscored India’s commitment to global partnerships through initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance, the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure and the Global Biofuels Alliance. She also reaffirmed India’s support for Small Island Developing States.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Today is World Cotton Day. This day is celebrated annually on October 7 to highlight the global economic, social, and environmental importance of cotton. The theme for this year is Cotton for Good: Building Prosperity Through Trade, Transformation and Partnership. Sharing a video message, Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh extended greetings to everyone associated with this sector.He said that this day honours farmers who cultivate cotton in the fields, thereby enabling employment for workers across the entire value chain, whether in spinning mills, ginneries, textile manufacturing units, or garment factories. He informed that 60 lakh farmers in the country are engaged in cotton cultivation. He underlined that countless small enterprises are linked to the handloom industries that not only operate domestically but also export their products.

. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics has been awarded to American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for developing macroeconomic models that help policymakers stabilise economies during booms and recessions. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said their work has strengthened the theoretical basis for fiscal and monetary policies and improved governments’ and central banks’ ability to respond to economic fluctuations.The Nobel Committee said, the economists developed models based on how households and businesses make decisions about spending, saving, investment and pricing, taking future economic conditions into account. Their research has helped policymakers understand how government policies and central bank signals influence economic activity. The models are now widely used by central banks and governments around the world.Robert E. Hall is a professor at Stanford University, while Michael Woodford is a professor at Columbia University. The prize carries an award of 12 million Swedish kronor, which will be shared equally between the two laureates.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has offered prayers to Maa Kushmanda, marking the fourth day of Navratri today. In a social media post, Mr Modi wished that her boundless energy bring new hope, happiness, prosperity and good health into the lives of all citizens.

. Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya today inaugurated the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games 2026 at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports organised the games in collaboration with the Gujarat Government.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Dr. Mandaviya emphasised that traditional and indigenous sports serve as a vital bridge, preserving cultural identity while unlocking new opportunities for global collaboration. The Minister added that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, initiatives like Khelo India are fostering a sustainable sports ecosystem from the grassroots to the international level.Mentioning upcoming international events in Ahmedabad, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi proposed five key initiatives for BRICS nations to preserve indigenous sports, including creatinga joint multilingual digital archive and integrating traditional games into academic curricula.Designed as a non-competitive platform, the Games brought together delegations from member and partner countries who presented a diverse range of indigenous sports.
